hints: Focus on what happens to the gases in the middle vessel if you change its pressure or remove one of its reactants.
Opening tap A lets the gases expand into an empty vessel, so total pressure falls and the equilibrium favours the side with more gas moles.
Opening tap B lets nitrogen escape to react with lithium, so think about which way the ammonia equilibrium must shift to replace lost nitrogen.
walkthrough:
**Recall the equilibrium in the middle vessel**

Think of this as a balanced tug of war that is easily disturbed. The reaction is:

$$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$$

Left side has 4 moles of gas, right side has only 2 moles of gas.

**Consider opening A to the evacuated vessel**

Opening A connects to empty space, so the gases spread out into double the volume. Pressure drops.

By Le Chatelier, a pressure drop favours the side with more gas molecules to try to raise pressure again. That is the left side, $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$. So $\text{NH}_3$ is used up and decreases.

**Consider opening B to the lithium vessel**

Lithium is special because it reacts with nitrogen even at room temperature:

$$6\text{Li}(\text{s}) + \text{N}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{Li}_3\text{N}(\text{s})$$

This removes $\text{N}_2$ from the equilibrium mixture. By Le Chatelier, removing a reactant pulls the equilibrium to the left to replace it. Again $\text{NH}_3$ breaks down, so ammonia decreases.

**Choose the action that keeps most ammonia**

Both opening A and opening B shift the equilibrium left and destroy ammonia, one by lowering pressure and one by removing nitrogen. Doing nothing leaves the original equilibrium undisturbed, so the most $\text{NH}_3$ remains.

options.A: Keeping both taps closed causes no change in volume, pressure or concentration. The equilibrium $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$ stays where it was, so no ammonia is lost to a left shift. This retains the most ammonia.
options.B: Opening both causes two left shifts at once. Expansion into the evacuated vessel lowers pressure and favours 4 moles over 2 moles, while lithium removes $\text{N}_2$ as solid $\text{Li}_3\text{N}$. Both effects destroy ammonia.
options.C: Opening A only still hurts. The gas volume doubles and pressure halves. The system shifts left toward $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$ because that side has more gas moles, so ammonia amount falls by dilution and by shift.
options.D: Opening B only still hurts. $\text{N}_2$ diffuses to the right and is trapped as solid $\text{Li}_3\text{N}$. Removing $\text{N}_2$ pulls the ammonia equilibrium left to make more $\text{N}_2$, which uses up $\text{NH}_3$.
